subject.title: Feature: Granular Discord action gates (split actions.messages into read/edit/delete)

question: Should OpenClaw add a backward-compatible per-operation Discord message permission model, and if so which legacy-boolean and omitted-field defaults should govern existing deployments?
rationale: This adds a public configuration and authorization contract whose defaulting rules determine whether existing agents retain, lose, or gain message capabilities after upgrade.

options.title: Approve granular gates with legacy fallback
options.body: Add explicit send, read, edit, and delete permissions while resolving absent subfields from the existing boolean so current configurations preserve their behavior.

options.title: Retain the coarse gate
options.body: Keep the single messages permission and document that deployments needing stronger separation must use Discord-side role restrictions or a future approved policy model.

options.title: Choose a narrower destructive-only gate
options.body: Add only a separately configurable delete permission if maintainers want the smallest new surface rather than a full per-operation matrix.

recommendation.title: Approve granular gates with legacy fallback
recommendation.body: Add explicit send, read, edit, and delete permissions while resolving absent subfields from the existing boolean so current configurations preserve their behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The available review history shows steipete as the clearest maintainer-side routing candidate for the unresolved Discord permission-contract decision.
